title: Scalar function that cannot be inlined, called in SELECT and WHERE
prompt: Nightly export of high-value customers per region. For region 3 (about 264k active customers) it runs about
14 minutes. sys.sql_modules.is_inlineable is 0 for qe.fn_CustomerNetPaid12m because it calls SYSDATETIME(). The
about 528k executions per run at about 1.6 ms each. Analysts sometimes run it with @MinNetPaid = 0 to get the full
list, including customers with no payments. Finance reconciles the output, so values (to the cent) and row
membership must not change. Other code uses the function, so it must stay as it is. The function is in the
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.

Payments: 60M rows. Status: Settled 88%, Failed 6%, Refunded 4% (negative Amount), Pending 2%. ExternalRef is NULL for ~30%; non-NULL values are almost unique, with a few duplicates from provider retries. Partner accounts have up to 180k Settled or Refunded payments each. Settlement batches stamp the same PaidAt on 50-500 payments.

correct_families.description: One aggregate over Payments for the region, outer-joined to the customers, rounded to decimal(19,2) before the comparison.
reference_sql: JOIN qe.Orders   o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN qe.Payments p ON p.OrderID = o.OrderID
LEFT JOIN Net n ON n.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
CROSS APPLY (SELECT CAST(ISNULL(n.NetRaw, 0) AS decimal(19,2)) AS NetPaid12m) x

traps.why: The function returns decimal(19,2), so it rounds the sum. Comparing the unrounded sum treats 99.995 differently at a threshold of 100.00 and returns four decimals.
traps.told_apart_by: A customer whose 12-month sum is 999.9950 with @MinNetPaid = 1000.
example_sql: JOIN qe.Orders   o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN qe.Payments p ON p.OrderID = o.OrderID
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, c.LastName, ISNULL(n.NetRaw, 0) AS NetPaid12m
LEFT JOIN Net n ON n.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE c.RegionID = @RegionID AND c.IsActive = 1 AND ISNULL(n.NetRaw, 0) >= @MinNetPaid

traps.why: Customers with no qualifying payment have a net of 0 and must appear when @MinNetPaid is 0 or less.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case region3_full_list: customers with no payment in 12 months disappear.
example_sql: JOIN qe.Orders   o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN qe.Payments p ON p.OrderID = o.OrderID
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber, c.LastName, CAST(n.NetRaw AS decimal(19,2)) AS NetPaid12m
JOIN Net n ON n.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE c.RegionID = @RegionID AND c.IsActive = 1 AND CAST(n.NetRaw AS decimal(19,2)) >= @MinNetPaid

traps.why: Other code calls the function. The task is to stop calling it here.
example_sql: JOIN qe.Orders   o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN qe.Payments p ON p.OrderID = o.OrderID
LEFT JOIN Net n ON n.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
CROSS APPLY (SELECT CAST(ISNULL(n.NetRaw, 0) AS decimal(19,2)) AS NetPaid12m) x

traps.why: Any form that still calls the function runs it once per row in a serial plan.
example_sql: CROSS APPLY (SELECT qe.fn_CustomerNetPaid12m(c.CustomerID) AS NetPaid12m) f
WHERE c.RegionID = @RegionID AND c.IsActive = 1 AND f.NetPaid12m >= @MinNetPaid

min_improvement.basis: 528k function calls at 1.6 ms each are the 14 minutes. One parallel aggregate must be at least ten times faster.

key.reference_notes: The function reads SYSDATETIME() on each call, so its 12-month boundary moves by milliseconds during the run. The rewrite uses one value for the whole statement. State that difference to the owner.
